tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM calls, chain executions, agent traces, prompt versions, and token usage across LangChain and non-LangChain applications
features: Token and cost tracking per run
tools.pricing: Free tier: 5,000 traces/month. Developer: $39/month for 50,000 traces. Plus: $150/month for 200,000 traces. Enterprise: custom pricing
tools.best_for: Teams building LangChain or complex multi-step LLM pipelines who need deep debugging, evaluation, and prompt management in a single platform

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, response times, token consumption, costs, error rates, and user-level usage across OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, and other providers
features: One-line proxy integration requiring minimal code changes
Request and response logging with search
Rate limiting and caching to reduce costs
tools.pricing: Free tier: 100,000 requests/month. Pro: $20/month for 1M requests. Team: $100/month for 5M requests. Enterprise: custom pricing
tools.best_for: Developers who want fast, low-friction observability by routing requests through a proxy, especially for cost monitoring and caching across multiple LLM providers

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: Model training metrics, LLM fine-tuning runs, prompt experiments, evaluation results, system resource usage, and production inference logs
features: LLM-specific Prompts and Traces UI (W&B Weave)
Integration with PyTorch, HuggingFace, and major ML frameworks
tools.pricing: Free tier: unlimited projects for individuals. Team: $50/user/month. Enterprise: custom pricing. Academic and open-source plans available
tools.best_for: ML teams that train, fine-tune, and evaluate LLMs and want a unified platform covering the full ML lifecycle from experimentation to production monitoring

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Model performance, data drift, embedding quality, LLM hallucinations, retrieval quality for RAG, token costs, and latency in production environments
features: RAG pipeline evaluation and retrieval quality scoring
A/B testing for prompt and model versions
Slice-and-dice analytics for performance by segment
Integration with LlamaIndex, LangChain, and custom stacks
tools.pricing: Free tier available with limited data retention. Growth: starts around $50/month. Enterprise: custom pricing based on volume and features
tools.best_for: Enterprise ML and data science teams that need rigorous production monitoring, drift detection, and evaluation for both traditional ML models and LLM-powered applications

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, token usage, costs, latency, prompt versions, user sessions, and evaluation scores across any LLM provider or framework
features: Detailed tracing with nested span support
Prompt management and versioning with SDK integration
Cost and token tracking per model and per user
Evaluation framework with human and automated scoring
Session and user-level grouping for analytics
SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and REST API
Integration with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and raw API calls
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosted: free. Cloud Hobby: free with limited retention. Cloud Pro: $59/month. Enterprise cloud or on-premise: custom pricing
tools.best_for: Teams that prioritize open-source transparency, self-hosting for data privacy, and need a cost-effective but feature-rich observability and evaluation platform

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token usage, latency, and errors using OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation across OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and other providers
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM libraries with minimal code
Compatible with any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend (Jaeger, Grafana, Datadog, etc.)
Traces LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, and direct API calls
Token and cost metadata attached to spans
Framework-agnostic design for flexible stack integration
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free. Costs depend on the observability backend you export data to (e.g., Grafana Cloud, Datadog, or self-hosted Jaeger)
tools.best_for: Engineering teams already invested in OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want to add LLM observability without adopting a new proprietary platform or vendor

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and semantic caching: use tools like Helicone or Redis-based caches to detect semantically similar requests and return cached responses, which can reduce API call volume by 20-60% for applications with repetitive query patterns

Right-size your model selection by routing requests based on complexity: use smaller, cheaper models like GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku for simple classification, summarization, or FAQ tasks, and reserve expensive frontier models only for complex reasoning tasks, cutting costs by up to 90% on simpler workloads

Optimize prompt length aggressively by auditing and trimming system prompts, removing redundant examples, and compressing context windows through summarization of long conversation histories, since token costs scale linearly and bloated prompts are one of the most common sources of unnecessary spend

Set hard budget limits and per-user rate limits using your observability platform or directly via API provider settings, and instrument cost alerting so you detect and respond to runaway usage, infinite loops in agents, or abuse patterns before they result in large unexpected bills
